description: Drop unlinked income, group the rest by linked member, then compute shares, the average share, and summarise the above-average groups.

c.request: Total up income `amount` by member (`link_to_member`) and work out each total's share of the sum of all the totals. For those whose share is strictly above the average share, give one row with: their combined amount, their average share, and the average amount by which their share is above the average share. No rounding. Drop unlinked income, group the rest by linked member, then compute shares, the average share, and summarise the above-average groups.
c.sql:
WITH income_grouped AS (
  SELECT 
    link_to_member,
    SUM(amount) as member_total
  FROM income
  WHERE link_to_member IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY link_to_member
),
all_stats AS (
  SELECT
    SUM(member_total) as grand_total,
    COUNT(*) as member_count
  FROM income_grouped
),
member_shares AS (
  SELECT
    ig.member_total,
    ig.member_total / ast.grand_total as share,
    1.0 / ast.member_count as average_share
  FROM income_grouped ig
  CROSS JOIN all_stats ast
),
above_avg AS (
  SELECT
    member_total,
    share,
    average_share
  FROM member_shares
  WHERE share > average_share
)
SELECT
  SUM(member_total) as combined_amount,
  AVG(share) as average_share,
  AVG(share - average_share) as average_above_average_amount
FROM above_avg

d.request: Group income by member (excluding records where link_to_member is NULL), sum amounts per member, calculate each member's share as their sum divided by total income, compute average share as one divided by count of distinct members, identify members with share strictly above average share, and output one row per such member with their combined amount, the average share value, and the excess of their share above the average share.
d.sql: WITH income_by_member AS (SELECT link_to_member, SUM(amount) as total_amount FROM income WHERE link_to_member IS NOT NULL GROUP BY link_to_member), total_income AS (SELECT SUM(amount) as total_sum FROM income WHERE link_to_member IS NOT NULL), member_count AS (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT link_to_member) as distinct_members FROM income WHERE link_to_member IS NOT NULL), member_shares AS (SELECT ibm.link_to_member, ibm.total_amount, ibm.total_amount / ti.total_sum as member_share, 1.0 / mc.distinct_members as avg_share FROM income_by_member ibm CROSS JOIN total_income ti CROSS JOIN member_count mc) SELECT total_amount, avg_share, member_share - avg_share as excess FROM member_shares WHERE member_share > avg_share

b.request: Group non-null income by member, identify those with above-average share, output one row with: combined income amount, average of above-average members' shares, and average excess above overall mean share.
b.sql:
WITH member_income AS (
    SELECT 
        SUM(amount) as member_total
    FROM income
    WHERE amount IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY link_to_member
),
all_stats AS (
    SELECT 
        SUM(member_total) as combined_income,
        AVG(member_total) as overall_avg
    FROM member_income
)
SELECT 
    all_stats.combined_income,
    (SELECT AVG(mi.member_total) 
     FROM member_income mi
     WHERE mi.member_total > all_stats.overall_avg) as avg_above_average_share,
    (SELECT AVG(mi.member_total - all_stats.overall_avg)
     FROM member_income mi
     WHERE mi.member_total > all_stats.overall_avg) as avg_excess_above_mean
FROM all_stats
b.raw: Group non-null income by member, identify those with above-average share, output one row with: combined income amount, average of above-average members' shares, and average excess above overall mean share.

a.request: Group the income records by linked member (`income.link_to_member`), after first dropping every income record whose `link_to_member` is missing, so such income plays no part in anything below. Sum `amount` in each group. Each group's share is its sum divided by the sum of all the group sums; then take the plain average of the shares across groups. Keep only groups whose share is strictly greater than that average, and return one row with: (1) the total of their summed amounts, (2) the average of their shares, and (3) the average of (share minus average share). Do not round.
a.sql: WITH income_filtered AS (SELECT link_to_member, amount FROM income WHERE link_to_member IS NOT NULL), group_sums AS (SELECT link_to_member, SUM(amount) as group_sum FROM income_filtered GROUP BY link_to_member), total_sum AS (SELECT SUM(group_sum) as total_amount FROM group_sums), shares AS (SELECT gs.link_to_member, gs.group_sum, CAST(gs.group_sum AS REAL) / CAST(ts.total_amount AS REAL) as share FROM group_sums gs CROSS JOIN total_sum ts), avg_share AS (SELECT AVG(share) as avg_share_value FROM shares), above_average AS (SELECT s.link_to_member, s.group_sum, s.share FROM shares s CROSS JOIN avg_share a WHERE s.share > a.avg_share_value) SELECT SUM(aa.group_sum) as total_amount, AVG(aa.share) as average_share, AVG(aa.share - (SELECT avg_share_value FROM avg_share)) as average_deviation FROM above_average aa
